title: The Tech Industry’s Aggressive Push to Integrate AI Into Schools Is Turning Into a Disaster
key_facts: Futurism's piece rests on Wall Street Journal reporting about students whose grades fell after using Google's AI tools provided through school computers.
A Pennsylvania eighth-grader, Richard Scott, told the WSJ Google's AI 'slowed my thinking down' and he failed his eighth-grade math final after B-range grades earlier.
Miami art history teacher Kaitlyn Ruano told the WSJ grades dropped after her district gave every student Google's Gemini chatbot.
A 15-year-old, Sophia Chatzigianni, said her grades fell while relying on Google's AI to summarise material and improved after she stopped.
Futurism frames this as part of a decades-long Google strategy to build a 'pipeline of future users' through schools, citing 2014 email scanning and 2018 internal documents.
The date of the underlying WSJ report is not given.
quote_evidence: “It slowed my thinking down,” Pennsylvania eighth-grader Richard Scott told the WSJ about Google’s AI assistant.
In Miami, art history teacher Kaitlyn Ruano told the WSJ she watched as student grades plummeted after the school district rolled out Google’s Gemini chatbot to every student.
why_it_matters_hint: Anecdotal WSJ accounts of students' grades falling after schools handed them Google's AI tools.
notes: Opinion-toned secondary piece; facts come from an undated WSJ report of a handful of cases, no systematic data. Headline ('disaster') overstates the evidence.
